classifiedFindings.title: Orphaned vault value after last relinquishPrincipal: relinquishing until totalDeposited==0 while getTotalShares()>0 freezes residual value, capturable in full by the next single depositor's skim
classifiedFindings.plausibility: n/a (not a High; no external attack scenario)

classification.assetImpact: No external asset theft or protocol loss. The value at risk is the relinquisher's OWN already-released principal. While totalDeposited==0 the residual is FROZEN (_skimSurplus early-returns on td==0); on the first subsequent deposit that depositor's totalBalanceOf momentarily inflates to (totalValue * principal)/totalDeposited and a following skimSurplus delivers the full residual to a protocol-owned recipient/next-depositor. Both relinquish entry points are privileged (relinquishPrincipal: onlyAuthorizedClient; relinquishPrincipalAsOwner: onlyOwner), and the authorized-client set is onlyOwner-curated (setClient is onlyOwner) — i.e. clients are protocol-owned, not external. Tier-3 fuzzing (128k calls, both strategies) confirms NO value is created and value-conservation holds: this is mis-attribution/sequencing inside the protocol's own books, not insolvency and not a leak to an external party.
attackPath: 1. (Privileged, self-inflicted) The LAST remaining authorized client calls relinquishPrincipal repeatedly (or owner calls relinquishPrincipalAsOwner) until clientBalances and totalDeposited reach 0 while getTotalShares() > 0 (shares deliberately untouched by relinquish).
2. Residual vault value is now orphaned and FROZEN: _skimSurplus early-returns while totalDeposited == 0, so no skim can distribute it.
3. A fresh deposit re-enters principal; that single depositor's totalBalanceOf = (totalValue * principal)/totalDeposited momentarily reflects the ENTIRE residual position.
4. A subsequent skimSurplus delivers the full residual to the recipient/next-depositor — who is a protocol-owned, owner-curated client, NOT an external attacker.
classification.likelihood: low — requires the last remaining client to fully relinquish its own principal to zero while live residual shares remain; an unusual, self-inflicted owner/keeper operational sequencing, reachable only via privileged (onlyAuthorizedClient/onlyOwner) calls. No permissionless trigger.
classification.assumptions: Authorized clients are owner-curated and protocol-owned (verified: setClient is onlyOwner). Residual value conservation holds (verified by Tier-3 128k-call fuzz, both strategies). The relinquish primitive (story-045) intentionally leaves vault shares untouched.
classification.externalRequirements: None that benefit an external party — there is no external attacker. The 're-capture' beneficiary is itself an owner-curated protocol-owned client. No value crosses the protocol boundary.

classifiedFindings.lawBasis: Law-3 non-obvious owner/integrator footgun. Surprise test PASSES: a competent, non-malicious integrator sequencing relinquish-to-zero with live residual shares would be surprised that the residual is frozen and then handed in full to the first re-depositor. Parked visibly per Law-1 (no silent drop); reported as an operational hazard with safe-config guidance, NOT as a malicious-owner vector.
classifiedFindings.documentationCheck: NOT-BLESSED. IYieldStrategy NatSpec (L34-41) blesses the share-untouched write-down and value-to-yield re-attribution 'ON RECOVERY' but presumes a surviving recovery path (a remaining client); it does NOT document the totalDeposited==0-with-shares orphan + re-capture-on-redeposit edge. No designDecision (incl. #2 requested-not-received, which is a WITHDRAW-path rule) and no systemAssumption covers it. knownIssuesCount=0.

severityRationale.notHigh: No assets stolen/lost/compromised and no valid external attack path. All triggers are privileged (onlyAuthorizedClient/onlyOwner); the value at risk is the relinquisher's own released principal; the beneficiary is a protocol-owned client; value-conservation holds (Tier-3). Upgrading to High would require an external theft/loss path that does not exist here.
severityRationale.notMedium: C4 Medium requires protocol function/availability impairment OR value leak to an external party with stated assumptions. Neither is present: protocol availability is not impaired (the residual is recoverable the instant principal re-enters; the system continues to function for deposits/withdraws), and no value leaks outside the protocol's own books. The mis-attribution is internal and self-inflicted by a privileged actor.
severityRationale.landsQaLow: State-handling / operational-sequencing footgun with a non-obvious consequence (Law-3). Maps to C4 QA/Low: 'state handling' / spec-sequencing hazard, surfaced with safe-config guidance.

classifiedFindings.recommendation: Either dispose/redeem the proportional vault shares on relinquish, or prevent totalDeposited from reaching 0 while getTotalShares() > 0 (sweep/attribute the residual to a protocol sink), or document the sequencing hazard with safe-config guidance so an integrator never relinquishes-to-zero while live residual shares remain.
classifiedFindings.justification: Privileged, self-inflicted state-handling footgun with no external theft path and no value leak outside the protocol; value-conservation verified by Tier-3. Correctly held at QA/Low (Law-3 non-obvious operational hazard) — not Medium (no availability/function impairment, no external value leak) and not High (no asset theft/loss, no external attacker).
classifiedFindings.noOverstatement: Confirmed. Held at the floor the impact supports; not upgraded.

classifiedFindings.title: Integration assumption for deferred stable-staker M-05 wiring: caller MUST pay-out/write-off principal to its end user BEFORE calling relinquishPrincipal and MUST NOT re-credit the resulting reflax surplus to the same owner (else cross-protocol double-count)

classification.assetImpact: Potential cross-protocol double-count of principal IF a future stable-staker caller credits the reflax surplus to the same owner whose principal it already paid out/wrote off. No current asset impact: the relinquishPrincipal primitive is staged ahead of its consumer and NO stable-staker callsite exists at this commit.
attackPath: 1. (Future, hypothetical — no callsite today) stable-staker wires relinquishPrincipal as the reflax-side of its deferred M-05 pro-rata-haircut fix.

2. If that wiring relinquishes principal WITHOUT first paying-out/writing-off the principal to the end user, OR re-credits the freed reflax surplus to the same owner, the same value is counted on both sides of the integration.
3. This would surface as a value mis-statement at the stable-staker boundary — but only once the constraint is actually violated by real wiring.
classification.likelihood: not assessable at this commit — there is no callsite and no demonstrated root cause in the current code. Filing at H/M would be 'speculation on future code without demonstrated root cause' (explicitly known-invalid).
classification.assumptions: Binds to the deferred stable-staker M-05 (fingerprint 0dca43f3, valid Medium, owner-accepted, pro-rata-haircut fix DEFERRED pending exactly this reflax relinquishPrincipal story).
classification.externalRequirements: Requires the stable-staker integration to land AND to violate the pay-out-then-relinquish / no-double-credit constraint. Until then there is no current exploit.

classifiedFindings.lawBasis: Law-2 cross-protocol faithfulness/integration constraint. Recorded (not dropped) per Law-1 so the constraint is audited when the wiring lands. Tagged faithfulness:true and routed to the spec-conformance channel (NOT buried in the QA/gas bundle).
classifiedFindings.documentationCheck: NOT-A-KNOWN-ISSUE and not suppressible. knownIssuesCount=0; no designDecision/systemAssumption documents a cross-protocol double-count guard. Distinct from existing spec-conformance entries F-01 (provable-solvency overstated) and F-02 (IYieldStrategy NatSpec staleness).

severityRationale.notHighOrMedium: No callsite and no demonstrated root cause at this commit; raising H/M now is 'speculation on future code' (known-invalid per CLAUDE.md). Held below H/M deliberately.
severityRationale.landsSpecConformance: Forward-looking cross-protocol integration constraint with security relevance but no current trigger -> recorded as a spec-conformance / informational carryover (F-label), visible to the owner, to be re-evaluated at Medium IF/WHEN the stable-staker caller wiring lands and violates the pay-out-then-relinquish constraint.
severityRationale.deferredEscalation: Re-evaluate at MEDIUM severity at the stable-staker integration point (a cross-protocol value double-count is value-leak-with-stated-assumptions territory), NOT this run.

classifiedFindings.recommendation: Record in spec-conformance.md, bound to deferred stable-staker M-05. When stable-staker wires relinquishPrincipal: assert the caller pays-out/writes-off principal to the end user BEFORE relinquishing, and does NOT re-credit the reflax surplus to the same owner. Re-evaluate at Medium severity at that integration point.
classifiedFindings.justification: Cross-protocol integration constraint (Law-2) with no current callsite; filing at H/M would be speculation on future code (known-invalid). Correctly classified as a spec-conformance / informational carryover, deferred to a Medium re-evaluation at the stable-staker integration point.
classifiedFindings.noOverstatement: Confirmed. Explicitly NOT raised to H/M; held as spec-conformance carryover with a deferred Medium gate.
